scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Pursere Kattuna is a traditional ritualistic dance form performed by Tulu-speaking people from various castes across different parts of Belthangady taluk.
It is a living heritage practice of Tulunadu, showcasing the folk imagination of Tulu society and preserving oral narratives, mythic storytelling, and seasonal practices.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The performance is held during the full moon in the month of Suggi according to the Tulu calendar.
Dancers visit the homes of people belonging to different social strata, blessing them with healing, prosperity and protection.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The musical instruments used in Pursa Kattuna includes Tase, Dolu, Nadaswara, Shruti.
These instruments guide the rhythm of the dance, mythic dialogues and singing sequences throughout the night.
Listen for the Tase, Dolu, Nadaswara, Shruti.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Pursa Kattuna uses a wide range of costumes and roles representing various castes, professions, mythic figures and social archetypes.

Costumes may depict Brahmins, priests, mendicants, ascetics, fortune tellers, Koti Chennaya, wild animals including bears, tiger, lion, monkey, scholars, thieves, ghosts, spiritual entities, and Christian or Muslim characters.

scenes.title: The people
narration: A similar type of performance exists in the Sullia region, but it uses a different costume style known as Siddavesha.
The style shows influence from the Natha Pantha spiritual tradition.
